verdicts.reason: A is a sensible banner split with the shoe on the left and copy on the right, and the headline and CTA are clear. But 'DROP 07' has moved below the body copy, so the eyebrow reads out of order, the body copy leaves an orphaned 'then gone.', the logo is tiny in the corner, and the panel runs off the right edge. B shrinks the shoe and pushes it against the left edge, where it is cut off. Its CTA button and the 'DROP 07' text are illegibly small, and the logo sits in the same row as the CTA and competes with it, which buries the call to action.

A is the same output as pair 1 B. The shoe is small and cut off at the left edge, the 'Enter the Draw' button is so tiny it can't be read, 'DROP 07' is microscopic, and the logo crowds the CTA row. B has a strong headline and a legible CTA with the shoe large on the right. Its flaws: the panel bleeds off the left edge, 'DROP 07' sits below the body copy instead of above the headline, the body leaves an orphaned 'then gone.', and the logo is undersized.

In A the shoe's toe is clipped behind the panel. The headline breaks awkwardly onto two lines, and 'DROP 07' is nearly as heavy as the headline, so the two compete. The CTA and logo are stranded in a separate right-hand column away from the copy, which scatters the grouping. B is the same weak layout as before: the shoe is cut off, the CTA and 'DROP 07' are illegibly tiny, and the logo competes with the CTA. A is less bad because its text and CTA can at least be read.
